body: This has been a bottom-up rebuild. The first battle was the starting position — back straight, chest open, elbows out, lats on — and for weeks the hips would shoot up early because the back tension wasn't holding. That got fixed in stages: opening the knees and consciously leading with the chest held the back angle (and produced my best snatch to date at 37), and then on the pulls I found that opening my stance a few inches lets my rib cage fit between my thighs — the back stays flatter and for the first time the lats genuinely engage. The bar feels lighter off the floor now; I still need to bring that setup into the snatch itself. So the fight has moved upstairs: the third-pull rhythm (elbow → arm → wrist) isn't flowing, and my wrists stay vertical instead of settling back overhead — the lockout feels wrong, and it cost me a rep at 37 (bar drifted forward). Same weight as a month ago, but the reps get honest — and the fault list keeps moving higher up the lift.

The clean has gone from my problem lift to my favourite — three doubles at 60 are now a working set, cues holding, with faster elbows and more back engagement as the next layer. The jerk is where the work is, and the story there has narrowed. First it was the dip: I kept drifting forward of vertical, and "head to the ceiling" largely fixed that. Now it's the split itself: my glutes weren't engaging, so the back leg stayed stiff and pole-vaulted my weight onto the front foot — which is also where the soft press-outs at the top end come from. The breakthrough was finding the internal cue: on behind-the-neck jerks I stayed at 50 to test consciously switching the glute on, and the split immediately improved. Off the back of that I hit 57 — my best clean & jerk ever, on the third attempt at the weight. Next: making the glute engagement automatic, and getting into the split faster.
